app.title: PEM Electrolysis Cell Designer (PEM-EC Designer)
app.summary: A person picks the cell's materials from preset libraries, then sets the operating conditions, stack geometry and coolant limits with sliders in a sidebar. A physical model recomputes everything at once: headline metrics for the stack, the cell's voltage curve split into its losses, a Tafel plot, stack voltage and power curves, and the heat balance with the coolant flow it needs. In an assembly tab they pick the other stack hardware and see a to-scale cross-section and a top view of the flow field, with stack height, mass, pressure drop and pump power. Last, they download the curve and an operating-point summary as CSV, and the assembly as JSON that can be loaded again.

task.text: Size an electrolyser cell and stack before building it, by choosing materials, operating point and geometry and reading the predicted voltage, power, output, heat and hardware dimensions.

data.text: A design configuration (materials picked from literature-referenced preset tables, operating conditions and geometry) put through a lumped physical model that gives performance curves over current density and quantities at the operating point.
data.item: one design configuration of a cell stack at one operating point

stage.text: early design sizing of an electrolyser stack, before detailed simulation or building

mechanism.text: The sidebar holds every input; whenever one changes, the whole model reruns and every tab redraws: the headline metrics, the curves with the operating point marked, the thermal and flow-field metrics, and the drawings of the assembly. The bipolar plate picked in the sidebar affects both the ohmic loss in the voltage curve and the assembly drawings.

field.text: lumped (0D) electrochemical modelling of PEM water electrolysis cells and stacks in engineering

workflow.name: size a design with a physical model by setting parameters and reading the predicted performance

steps.step: choose components from a library of presets
steps.here: Sidebar dropdowns choose the membrane, anode and cathode catalysts, the two gas diffusion layers and the bipolar plate. A hydration slider scales the membrane's water content, and captions show the conductivity and exchange current densities this gives at the set temperature.

steps.step: set the operating conditions and geometry
steps.here: Sliders and number fields set temperature, pressure, operating current density, cell count, active area, aspect ratio, allowed coolant temperature rise and coolant heat capacity.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The model gives stack voltage, power, hydrogen output, energy efficiency and waste heat at the operating point. A table splits the cell voltage into reversible voltage, activation, ohmic and concentration losses.

steps.step: look at how the result changes across the operating range
steps.here: There are curves of cell and stack voltage, power and heat against current density, with reference lines and the operating point marked, and a log-scale Tafel plot that compares full Butler-Volmer kinetics with the Tafel asymptote.

steps.step: check the design against physical limits
steps.here: The thermal tab gives the heat balance and the coolant flow needed, and warns when operation is endothermic. A flow-field block computes pressure drop, Reynolds number and pump power from a stoichiometric ratio and a pump efficiency, and warns when the flow is outside the laminar regime.

Dropdowns choose the end plate, current collector, gasket and tie-rod. A to-scale stack cross-section, with an exploded-view gap slider, and a top view of the plate's flow field are drawn, along with stack height, mass, plate size and open-area ratio.
Buttons download the polarization curve and the operating-point summary as CSV, and the assembly configuration as JSON. The JSON can be loaded back through the assembly tab's uploader.

distinctive: The cell voltage is built up from the reversible voltage plus separate loss terms, and each term is shown stacked on the curve and listed in a table at the operating point.
Material properties are corrected for the operating conditions before use: membrane conductivity from hydration and temperature, and catalyst exchange current from temperature by Arrhenius.
The thermoneutral voltage separates operating points that need cooling from those that need heating, and the coolant flow is sized from the allowed temperature rise.
A hardware choice affects both the electrical model and the to-scale mechanical drawing, so one choice changes both the voltage curve and the stack dimensions.
Every preset carries a literature reference, shown alongside its key properties.

parts.title: Design inputs sidebar
parts.summary: Collects all the model inputs: material presets, membrane hydration, operating conditions, stack geometry and coolant limits, with captions giving the derived properties.

parts.title: Stack headline metrics
parts.summary: Shows stack voltage, power, hydrogen output, energy efficiency and waste heat at the current operating point.

parts.title: Polarization and Tafel plots
parts.summary: Plots cell voltage against current density with each loss stacked on the reversible voltage, lists the voltage breakdown at the operating point, and compares Butler-Volmer activation losses with Tafel lines.

parts.title: Stack analysis
parts.summary: Plots stack voltage and electrical power against current density and lists the stack's quantities at the operating point.

parts.title: Thermal balance
parts.summary: Compares cell voltage with the thermoneutral voltage, sizes the coolant flow, warns when operation is endothermic, and plots waste heat against current density.

parts.title: Materials library
parts.summary: Lists the selected materials with their key properties and references, and expandable tables of every membrane and catalyst preset.

parts.title: Stack assembly designer
parts.summary: Chooses the stack hardware, draws a to-scale exploded cross-section and the plate's flow field, gives height, mass and plate size, computes pressure drop and pump power, and saves or loads the assembly as JSON.

parts.title: Export
parts.summary: Downloads the polarization curve and the operating-point summary as CSV files, named after the design parameters.
